source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22); (AJ) Military Retirement Credit (PDF p.23) and worksheet lines 1 and 2 (PDF p.24)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 1) 40,000.00 + military retirement pay (person 0) 30,000.00 + military retirement pay (person 1) 20,000.00 = 90,000.00. Federal taxable income = 90,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 58,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (married filing jointly): line 4 federal AGI 90,000.00. Line 5 additions: none, 0.00. Line 6 = 90,000.00 + 0.00 = 90,000.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 90,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 90,000.00. Line 10 = 90,000.00 x 0.045 = 4,050.00. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 31,500.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 90,000.00, cap 31,500.00) = 0.06 x 31,500.00 = 1,890.00. Line 17 base phase-out amount 36,426.00. Line 18 = max(0, 90,000.00 - 36,426.00) = 53,574.00. Line 19 = 53,574.00 x 0.013 = 696.462. Line 20 = max(0, 1,890.00 - 696.462) = 1,193.538. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 90,000.00; line 2 standard deduction 31,500.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 31,500.00; line 5 = max(0, 90,000.00 - 31,500.00) = 58,500.00. Line 5 is above zero, so not exempt; line 21 blank. TC-40A Part 3: Military Retirement Credit Worksheet: line 1 50,000.00; line 2 = 50,000.00 x 0.045 = 2,250.00. Line 22 and TC-40A Part 3: line 20 1,193.538 + AJ 2,250.000 = 3,443.538; credits 3,443.54. Tax = 4,050.00 - 3,443.54 = 606.46. One worksheet for each person; the two are added. Expected lines are the formula results rounded to the cent at the end (half up); the three-decimal figures above are unrounded.
